evidence: host/native/owner.lisp:5103-5122: `(fnn-state-checkpoint-write store (lambda (fd) ...)) ... (setq durablep t) ;; T8: the installed checkpoint covers the segments ... (fnn-log-drop store covered)` (the same pattern is at io.lisp:3462-3464 and owner.lisp:5781-5783). Against this, books/store-checkpoint-open.lisp:765-769 says `Otherwise the open is a full replay ... it is slower, never wrong, because the checkpoint is derived and replay stays authoritative (storage.md:227)`, and host/native/io.lisp:2783-2784 (fnn-state-checkpoint-write) says `a corrupt or missing one falls back to full replay.` But books/store-log-segments.lisp:261 gives `((not (member-equal 1 present)) (list :refused :checkpoint-damaged))`.
fix: Before fnn-log-drop, re-open the installed checkpoint from disk and verify it with the same reader the open uses (fn-store-sco-decode plus the arena run's chain). Drop only when that verify succeeds. Alternatively keep the previous checkpoint generation (or the segments covered by it) until a newer generation has been verified, so at least one verified older copy always survives. Then correct the comments in store-checkpoint-open.lisp:765-769 and io.lisp:2783-2784 to describe the post-drop reality.
reviewer: owner.lisp:5103-5122 installs the checkpoint and then calls fnn-log-drop on the covered segments. Nothing reads the installed file back first. Once segment 1 is gone and the checkpoint cannot be used, store-log-segments.lisp:261 refuses with :checkpoint-damaged, and io.lisp:7570-7590 says so itself: 'there is no full replay to fall back to'. Dropping the segments is intended (docs/glossary.md:21), so the defect is narrower than the report: the drop has no read-back before it, and two comments are now false. io.lisp:2783 ('a corrupt or missing one falls back to full replay') and store-checkpoint-open.lisp:765-769 ('slower, never wrong ... replay stays authoritative') still describe a fallback that no longer exists. Losing the store this way needs on-disk corruption, or an encoder/reader disagreement the per-frame checks miss, so I rate it medium rather than high.
scenario: The owner auto-publishes a checkpoint, renames it into place, fsyncs the directory and immediately unlinks segments 1..K-1. Nothing reads the installed file back from disk first. Suppose the file is later unreadable or fails its digest chain: a bad sector, a lying fsync, or an encoder/reader disagreement that the in-memory per-frame admission did not catch. fn-sco-select then answers :corrupt, which makes the open plan's FIRST nil, and fn-lgs-open-plan refuses :checkpoint-damaged. The store can never open again, because the whole article history (the arena run carries every payload) existed only in that one file. The rename also replaces the previous generation, so no older checkpoint is left either. This is the opposite of the documented 'slower, never wrong' fallback.
title: Covered log segments are dropped after every checkpoint with no read-back, so the checkpoint becomes the only copy of history, while the code and comments still say a corrupt checkpoint 'falls back to full replay'
